notes: Example configuration generated by the CraneCalc configurator; fictitious crane, supplier, survey and owner data, to be replaced with project data. Scope: 4 simply supported 45-ft bays, W36X529 girders, one 30-ton cab crane, on new welded haunched rib seats welded to the existing W14X159 columns, with the rail, ties, bearings and end stops; the existing columns are checked with their existing load effects and the existing sidewall rod bracing takes the crane longitudinal forces. The flexible plate cannot pass as sized (tie sizing ratio flange-tie-saddle-weld 2.24 > 1.00 for the estimated tie demands): the tie is paired flat bars on the same saddle, each bar taking half the force. A direct flange saddle does not suit this rolled girder (the sized saddle leaves flange-tie-saddle-weld 1.95, flange-tie-column 1.93 for the estimated tie demands): the tie is paired flat bars, which bolt to the tie-side bearing stiffener, cut as one plate with its gusset extension past the flange tip (no weld at the gusset), the full-depth stiffener pair carrying the tie force into the girder. Bumper overhang assumed 20 in (end-wheel centerline to the extended bumper face, a typical supplier proportion): the stop contact positions use it; confirm with the crane supplier.

Lightest compact W within the sizing targets (ratio ≤ 0.85, deflections ≤ 0.9 of the limits): top-flange tip stress (DG7, warping and second-order twist) ratio 0.82, vertical deflection 0.27 and lateral 0.36 of their limits; flanges at least 10.5 in wide for the end bearing bolt gauge and the rail seat; lighter candidates rejected: 147 by sizing ratio, 63 by flange width; the next lighter, W14X500: tips ratio 1.22 > 0.85; vertical deflection 1.28 of the limit > 0.9. fabrication.steel: Girder ASTM A992; plates, bars and stiffeners ASTM A572 Grade 50 unless noted.
fabrication.bolting: ASTM F3125 Grade A325, pretensioned, Class B faying surfaces, standard holes unless slots are detailed. Sliding-end bearing bolts and column-end tie bolts pretensioned against steel sleeves. Rail joints tight (gap 1/16 in max.) with the rail supplier's joint bars and bolts (deferred submittal), bolts pretensioned and re-tightened after 30 and 90 days of operation.
fabrication.welding: E70XX low-hydrogen electrodes per AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020, cyclically loaded provisions. Continuous fillets as dimensioned; no intermittent welds on cyclic load paths. Smooth starts and stops.
fabrication.inspection: Visual inspection of all welds; AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020 cyclically loaded acceptance criteria; magnetic particle testing of fillets at fatigue-sensitive attachments; 100% ultrasonic testing of CJP welds; bolt pretension verification per RCSC.
fabrication.erection: Set and level the bearings, install the end bearings and flange ties, then set the rails. Provide temporary restraint until the permanent ties are complete.
fabrication.railAlignment: Set the rails to the specified gauge, alignment and level tolerances and survey them after erection, before the load test.
